messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: gpu-thermal-alert triggered at 02:05 UTC -> node: compute-pool-9-node-03, severity: page, reason: rapid temp rise + ECC spikes
Alex: I'm on it. opening thread. who is live?
Sam: I'm up. pulling NVML & node metrics.
Jordan: joining, paging hw-ops. @Leah heads-up for customer comms if needed.
infra-bot: Auto-action: initiating graceful drain on compute-pool-9-node-03 (evict-grace=45s)
Sam: raw metrics: temp jumped 65->86C in ~4m, corrected ECC errors spiked (8 in 3m), fan duty increased to 100%
Sam: logs snippet:
``
[2026-04-02T02:03:40Z] nvml: ecc_corrected=8, gpu_temp=86C, fan_rpm=6800
[2026-04-02T02:04:05Z] kernel: thermal_zone: gpu_temp threshold exceeded
```
Alex: Any customer impact noted? checking route-maps and pax-leases
Jordan: Looks like one dedicated shard from BetaCorp on that node. BetaCorp saw ~1.2% request error bump between 02:03-02:09 (503/timeout). No public status page yet.
Leah: CS notified BetaCorp with a temporary note. No escalations.
Alex: Plan: cordon + drain (done), reschedule shards to compute-pool-9-node-{04,07}, check fan telemetry & power rails, create HW ticket if temp doesn't fall within 10m, and follow-up with alert tuning to reduce ephemeral pages.
Sam: cordoned and drained. pods moving. watch reschedule.
infra-bot: Node compute-pool-9-node-03 status: DRAINING -> DRAINED
Sam: temps trending down to mid-70s after pod evacuation. ECC corrections dropped to zero in last 4m. VRAM usage unaffected.
Alex: marking immediate page mitigated. moving to post-incident cleanup. We need to stop noisy pages from short ECC flurries.
Jordan: Proposal for ECC alert change: current: `sum(rate(nvml_gpu_ecc_corrected_total[1m])) > 3` -> new: `sum_over_time(increase(nvml_gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m])[5m]) > 6` and require `for: 8m` before paging. Also correlate with `avg_over_time(node_gpu_temp_celsius[8m]) > 82` for page severity.
Leah: Also add label-based suppression: if node_label_maintenance=true OR node_state=draining -> silence ECC pages (only send non-page alerts to channel).
Sam: VRAM OOM alerts are noisy during kube evictions. Suggest: change VRAM alert to trigger only when `gpu_memory_utilization > 92` for `for: 4m` and exclude `kube_pod_deletion_time` windows.
Alex: I'll add an alertmanager mute rule for the compute-pool-9 group while HW investigates: mute for 40m for pager notifications, keep slack warnings.
infra-bot: Alertmanager: muted receiver=pager for label pool=compute-pool-9 for 40m (applied)
Jordan: ops playbook update snippet to put in runbook:
- Acknowledge page, check nvml + dmesg
- If gpu_temp > 85C AND ecc_rate sustained > 5/5m -> cordon+drain
- Prioritize dedicated shard migration, track customer lease IDs
- If temps don't recover in 15m -> escalate to HW with serial + nvml dump
Alex: I'll PR the alert rule changes. Sam take VRAM tweak. Jordan file HW ticket with serial & logs. Leah send customer update after RCA drafted.
Sam: PR opened: github.com/redwood/alerting/pull/612 -> ECC alert 5m window + for:8m; VRAM change in separate commit.
Jordan: HW ticket created: HW-4487. attached nvml logs, kernel traces, and fan RPM history.
Leah: CS note posted to BetaCorp. included ETA and that Dedicated routing handled failover.
Alex: Merged ECC PR after review. Alertmanager reload scheduled. Also added temporary runbook note to oncall playbooks page.
infra-bot: ALERTMANAGER RELOAD: success
Sam: Grafana dashboard draft updated: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/gpu-health/prod-gpu-overview -> added panels: temp-trend, ecc-rate, vram-util with node drain annotation layer
Leah: Follow-ups/action items:
- [ ] Jordan: follow through on HW-4487 and confirm fan replacement or re-seat (due EOD)
- [ ] Sam: finalize VRAM alert PR and add eviction-aware filter (due next sprint)
- [ ] Alex: add mute-exception for draining nodes in alertmanager config and add to oncall runbook (due today)
- [ ] Leah: prepare RCA summary and CS communication (due today)
Jordan: uploaded nvml dumps and kernel logs to incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/gpu-thermal-2147001234
Alex: status: mitigated, customers restored, moving to postmortem. big thanks to the oncall crew.
Leah: nice work. closing thread but will reopen if HW finds persistent issues.
